findings.source_passage: so he lives in light. He makes his berth an Aladdin's lamp, and lays him down in it; so that in the pitchiest night the ship's black hull still houses an illumination.
findings.why_it_matters: The rhythmic cadence 'lays him down in it; so that in the pitchiest night the ship's black hull still houses an illumination' is the interpretive and imagistic climax of the paragraph — the contrast of black hull and internal light is a signature Melville figure. The draft cuts 'lays him down in it' and the entire 'pitchiest night / black hull / illumination' sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'He makes his berth an Aladdin's lamp, and lays him down in it; so that in the pitchiest night the ship's black hull still houses an illumination.'

findings.source_passage: a fluid unknown to solar, lunar, or astral contrivances ashore
findings.why_it_matters: This triplet — 'solar, lunar, or astral contrivances' — is stylistically distinctive, carrying Melville's mock-grandiose register and the thematic claim that whale-oil transcends all earthly illuminants. Its excision flattens the chapter's central conceit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore after 'unvitiated': 'a fluid unknown to solar, lunar, or astral contrivances ashore.'

findings.source_passage: even as the traveller on the prairie hunts up his own supper of game
findings.why_it_matters: The prairie-traveller simile closes the chapter with a distinctly American frontier analogy that reinforces the self-sufficiency motif; its loss mildly thins the rhetorical finish.
findings.suggested_fix: Append: 'even as the traveller on the prairie hunts up his own supper of game.'

summary: Two medium-severity losses — the 'pitchiest night / black hull / illumination' sentence and the 'solar, lunar, or astral contrivances' phrase — strip the chapter of its central imagistic and rhetorical signature, warranting regeneration.
